feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: clear positioning, solid progression, and relevant platform/strategy depth. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within the same organization, showing increasing scope, leadership, and trust.  
- Strong relevance for digital strategy roles: Drupal, analytics, governance, content operations, multimedia, and cross-channel communications are all well evidenced.  
- Writing is generally polished and specific, with credible examples such as the 10,000+ page migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity: e.g., email growth, engagement lifts, traffic improvements, production savings, adoption rates, or campaign results. Several bullets describe responsibilities more than impact.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these would tighten structure and make the CV easier to scan.  
- Minor language/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; maintain serial comma consistency (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs lists without final comma); “front-end” and “organization-wide” are consistent, but bullet punctuation/hyphen formatting in work entries is visually dense and could be cleaner.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s core themes, but it is slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with sharper positioning tied to senior leadership, public-sector/advocacy work, and measurable scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with seniority and sector relevance: emphasize digital strategy leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with tighter, higher-impact wording such as “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Add one concrete differentiator from recent roles, e.g., enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, or large-scale stakeholder publishing environments.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Expertise includes enterprise web modernization, cross-channel content operations, and the systems, governance, and analytics that support complex stakeholder environments. Strong background in advocacy messaging and translating policy or technical issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflows and systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” also appears throughout Work Experience; keep it here only if central to target roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize senior-level, differentiating capabilities rather than repeating general communications terms.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, higher-value terms: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Content operations & governance,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Reduce generic wording like “Multi-channel communication” and “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” in favor of more senior, outcome-oriented language.
- Group related items for consistency and scannability; suggested version: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Content operations & editorial governance • Cross-channel campaign communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & automation • Policy & advocacy messaging • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Keep style parallel: all noun phrases, consistent use of “&,” and avoid mixing broad functions with soft skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy,” “analytics,” “multimedia,” and “web/CMS” are already covered in more detail in Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level value, transformation scope, and 2–3 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope and client value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign delivery, and web operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper impact statements, e.g.:
- “Designed cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance improvements to streamline organization-wide communications.”
- “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and user discovery experience.”
- Replace generic phrases like “deliver CMS development” and “advise on best practices” with outcomes: faster publishing, improved findability, reduced manual work, stronger campaign reuse, etc.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages supported, launch dates, adoption by teams, engagement lift, search success, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media: governance, analytics, enterprise web improvement.
- Specific project details also duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization win and keep the metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email/social growth, engagement, CTR, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed as “built first in-house broadcast studio.”

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level and tighten generic phrases like “helped improve” and “strengthened.”

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving coordination of editorial and advocacy messaging.”
- Replace weak verbs with ownership: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across digital platforms.”
- Combine the last two bullets and add a measurable result if possible: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved consistency, turnaround time and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is very similar to the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize execution, workflow building and channel growth here instead of broad leadership.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this Topline Skills item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, executive-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Make the list more distinctive and outcome-oriented where possible:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable publishing systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Public-sector advocacy messaging and audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations and cross-team editorial planning” to better match the experience section.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid repeating “leadership” and “strategy” multiple times across skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” substantially duplicate Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already reinforced in the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and delivery leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing; lead with Drupal/CMS modernization since that aligns most directly with recent NACo work.
- Cut lower-signal or older items here (e.g., jQuery, possibly WordPress/SharePoint if not central to target roles) and group coding more concisely.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- Airtable-based content and operational systems
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented modifier such as “for high-volume public-sector websites” to reinforce scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic/capability-based and leave full tool inventory to the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; use slightly different wording or keep it in only one place.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language: “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than “Analytics, Insights & Optimization.”
- Replace the current line with: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • SEO, performance and user-behavior analysis”
- Order by strategic weight, not just software: KPI design and executive reporting should come before SEO/performance analysis.
- If space allows, add one impact-oriented phrase tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web decision-making”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.
- Tool list also repeats “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and less exhaustive.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and production scope rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to higher-value delivery language, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production & editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio operations & PTZ camera systems
- Virtual event and advocacy content delivery

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS depth or differentiated by proficiency/context.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise migration, governance, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Add light qualifiers only where they reinforce impact, e.g. “Drupal 10” if current/recent and accurate.
- If space allows, group by level: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint | Lightweight publishing: Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation detail for the coding/technical section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills > “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus modernization context.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere; consider removing if not strategically important.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add one specificity cue tied to recent work: “Drupal front-end implementation,” “analytics/tag deployment,” or “workflow/deployment automation.”
- Order by senior relevance: API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, then front-end languages.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may also fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more role-relevant by separating automation tools from collaboration/project tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strategic relevance: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Remove lower-value/redundant tools unless actively used recently: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers for impact: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana (project operations)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; this section should stay tool-focused, not repeat capability language.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep only if they support a broader operations/collaboration narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the level of ownership or use case shown elsewhere in the CV. It would be stronger if framed around enterprise email operations and member engagement systems rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten/standardize platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light context for scope: **Enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations and member engagement platforms**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating outcomes here.
- “Engagement” is broad and may blur with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep this item clearly focused on email/member communications platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with clearer scope and any available outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/reach of weekly video updates, or growth in production capacity.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and recurring video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Supported a major website refresh, expanded in-house multimedia production, and helped standardize cross-channel publishing operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” and workflow improvements overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on building the team/capability, not ongoing channel leadership.
- Avoid repeating website/email/social oversight language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy development.”
- Make the second sentence more active and specific: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: audience reached, number of episodes, stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy or member engagement.
- Consider trimming “contributed to” and “materials,” which weaken impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Podcast/multimedia work overlaps with later video and digital production roles; keep this entry focused on “first podcast” and innovation/research support, not general digital operations.
- Avoid broad claims about web/email/social here, since those are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
